# OpenDoc

<!-- The template for llms.txt. The prose here is written by a person; the page
     list under "Site pages" is generated from each page's own <title> and meta
     description by webapp/tools/build-seo.mjs, so a page is described once and a
     new page cannot be forgotten. Edit this file, then run
     ./tools/build-seo.mjs (build.sh does it, and --check fails on drift). -->

> OpenDoc is an open-source Rust document runtime for deterministic, loss-aware
> DOCX import, editing, layout, rendering, and export across native,
> WebAssembly, and headless hosts.

OpenDoc is developed by CasualOffice and licensed under Apache-2.0. The engine,
not the browser DOM, owns document state and layout. Host applications own
storage, network, authentication, fonts, telemetry, and product UI policy. No
server, React dependency, or collaboration provider is required.

OpenDoc is pre-release. It handles real DOCX documents and powers a live
client-side browser editor, but it is not yet a stable public SDK or a
pixel-perfect replacement for Microsoft Word. Consult the support matrix and
execution tracker before relying on a specific fidelity claim.

The current priority is DOCX fidelity. Future goals include a stable SDK
release, ODT/plain-text and other document-format support, and native PDF export
from the runtime's deterministic layout/display-list pipeline. These are roadmap
directions, not currently supported features.

## Site pages

<!-- Generated from each page's own <title> and meta description by
     webapp/tools/build-seo.mjs. Edit the page, not this list. -->
- [OpenDoc — build documents on an engine you control](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/): OpenDoc is a deterministic, open-source Word-document runtime written in Rust. Import, edit, lay out, render, and write .docx on native, WebAssembly, and headless hosts — with no required server, DOM, or UI framework.
- [Documentation — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/docs.html): Documentation for OpenDoc, the open-source Rust DOCX engine and embeddable WebAssembly editor: embedding, import, dispositions, architecture, and the reference docs.
- [Embed the editor — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/embedding.html): Embed the OpenDoc editor in your own page: an installable package, the <opendoc-editor> custom element, and a capability contract resolved before the frame's first navigation. Every example on this page is extracted from code that runs in CI.
- [DOCX fidelity support matrix — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/fidelity.html): OpenDoc fidelity, measured against a LibreOffice oracle rather than a feature list: page-count parity, round-trip disposition, and honest per-construct support. The oracle geometry gate is manual (workflow_dispatch) and currently inert — no reference is committed — so these grades are hand-checked, not CI-enforced.
- [Embed configuration playground — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/playground.html): Change a role, withhold a capability, take away a chrome region or supply a brand colour, and watch an embedded OpenDoc editor change with it — then copy the configuration that reproduces exactly what is on screen.
- [Target Architecture — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/architecture.html): The system is a headless document engine with host adapters. The DOM, React state, Tauri state, and canvas state are projections.
- [Context Menu and Shared Command Descriptors — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/command-registry.html): The web editor has a table-only right-click menu assembled from a private array. Prose, selections, links, lists, comments, and suggestions fall through to the browser menu.
- [Contributing — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/contributing.html): This repository is building a production-grade document runtime. Contributions should protect correctness, fidelity, security, performance, and maintainability.
- [Import Disposition Taxonomy — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/disposition-taxonomy.html): A single value per entry cannot express the outcome the fidelity architecture exists to serve: a construct can be partially mapped into the model and have its unconsumed remainder either retained in the preservation ledger or lost.
- [DOCX Package Reader — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/docx-package-reader.html): Add casual-doc-ooxml with a security-bounded, read-only DOCX package layer. This slice validates ZIP structure and exposes safe on-demand part reads.
- [Embeddability and the SDK, in three phases — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/embeddability-plan.html): Embeddability is the product (SKILL.md §1). ONLYOFFICE is AGPL-3.0-only, bills the Developer Edition per concurrent browser tab, and gates host customization in code — LayoutManager._applyCustomization early-returns when !_licensed.
- [Error Code Registry — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/error-code-registry.html): Error codes are never recycled. Message wording may improve without a breaking release, but code meaning may not.
- [Project Glossary — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/glossary.html): This glossary defines terms used by the OpenDoc runtime, SDK, tests, and documentation. Public API names should use these terms consistently.
- [Reference documentation — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/index.html): Every OpenDoc architecture, design and specification document published on this site, generated from the repository's own Markdown so a page and its source can never disagree. Documents deliberately not published here are named, with the reason, in webapp/tools/build-doc-pages.mjs.
- [PDF Export and Print Design — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/pdf-export-and-print.html): Absence from a support list is an overstatement by omission, so every family the display list can carry is listed here, including the ones that are not covered.
- [SDK API Specification — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/sdk-api-spec.html): The broad interfaces below describe the intended v1 facade and are not all implemented.
- [Security Policy — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/security.html): Do not open a public issue for a suspected vulnerability, malicious fixture, or confidential document. The project will acknowledge a complete report, assess severity, coordinate a fix and advisory, and credit the reporter when requested.

The browser editor is a WebAssembly application, not a document: it is reachable
from the pages above and is deliberately absent from sitemap.xml, because what it
renders to a crawler is application chrome rather than readable prose.

## Technical scope

- OOXML package admission with explicit path, size, expansion, and resource bounds.
- Normalized editable document model with styles, sections, tables, drawings,
  links, fields, notes, headers/footers, comments, revisions, bookmarks, and
  content controls.
- Semantic DOCX writer plus byte-identical reconstruction for unedited packages.
- Rust text shaping, pagination, display-list composition, CPU raster rendering,
  hit testing, model-anchored selection, command-based editing, and undo/redo.
- Rust-native, wasm32, and headless execution targets with host-populated font
  and resource seams.
